data.title: Safety & Wellness Work Group
data.description:
VENTURA COLLEGE MISSION STATEMENT: At Ventura College, we transform students’ lives, develop human potential, create an informed citizenry, and serve as the educational and cultural heart of our community. Placing students at the center of their learning experience, we serve a highly diverse student body by providing innovative instruction and student support, focusing on associate degree and certificate completion, transfer, workforce preparation, and basic skills. We are committed to the sustainable continuous improvement of our college and its services.
SAFETY AND WELLNESS WORKGROUP CHARGE: The Safety and Wellness Committee is a college advisory committee and alerts management, faculty, staff, and students of matters pertaining to campus safety and health related issues. Members review and update safety practices and recommend additional practices as needed. Committee members visually inspect campus buildings for Safety and/or Health related issues, which are reported to the committee for appropriate resolution. The committee actively promotes educational safety and dissemination of health-related information to the campus community.

data.title: VC Curriculum Committee Meeting
data.description:
Meeting held in Multidisciplinary Center West (MCW) 312
Written materials relating to a Curriculum Committee meeting item that are distributed to at least a majority of the Curriculum Committee members less than 72 hours before a noticed meeting and that are public record not otherwise exempt from disclosure will be available for inspection at Ventura College located at 4667 Telegraph Road, Ventura, CA 93003 or at the Curriculum Committee meeting.
Pursuant to the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act, if you require any special accommodation or assistance to attend or participate in the meeting, please direct your written request, as far in advance of the meeting as possible, to the office of: Vice President Academic Affairs - Ventura College - 4667 Telegraph Road, Ventura, CA 93003 - (805) 289-6380.
The mission of Ventura College's Curriculum Committee is to provide guidance, advocacy and oversight for VC's curriculum by ensuring that the curriculum is academically sound, comprehensive and responsible to the evolving needs of the community so that the college's mission, goals and educational delivery to students are well served. The Curriculum Committee is a subcommittee of the Academic Senate and is a shared governance committee.

data.title: OC Technology Effectiveness Committee
data.description:
The Technology Effectiveness Committee (TEC) supports and advances the college mission, vision, and values by assessing college needs related to technology planning, use, efficiency, development, and maintenance. The TEC makes recommendations to the College Planning Council.

TEC meets the Wednesday of the month the month during the Fall and Spring semesters.

data.title: OC Curriculum Committee
data.description: The Curriculum Committee supports and advances the college mission, vision, and values through recommending new and revised curriculum to the governing board of the District. The Curriculum Committee provides guidance, advocacy, and oversight in the development of courses, programs, and academic policies. It ensures that the curriculum is academically sound, comprehensive, and responsive to student needs. This committee directly supports the 10 + 1 of the Academic Senate.

data.title: VC Academic Senate Council Meeting
data.description:
Accessibility Statement

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and California Government Code Section 54953(g), The Ventura College Academic Senate will make every reasonable effort to accommodate persons with disabilities. If you require a disability-related modification or accommodation, please contact vcacademicsenate@vcccd.edu at least 24 hours before the meeting.

VCAS Goals 2026-2027

  • Communication: Improve communication between the Senate and the faculty it represents by establishing consistent expectations and procedures for reporting and gathering feedback.
  • Training: Strengthen a shared understanding of the Senate's role in accordance with the "10+1" and Title 5 principles and enable Senate members to work effectively by consistently applying Robert's Rules of Order (meeting procedures).
  • Engagement: Strengthen the connection between part-time faculty and the appointed part-time Senate representative so that engagement strategies are based on part-time faculty input.

10+1

The 10+1 refers to eleven academic and professional matters where California community college academic senates hold primary responsibility for recommendations under AB 1725.

VCAS Canvas Course

Self-enroll in VCAS Canvas Course for Senator Handbook, sub-committee information, workgroups, governance documents, and VCAS/college budget resources.
